sources.entry: Vane - Native WebKit browser with sidebar tabs, Spaces, and Split View, in early development for macOS 26 or later.

summary.one_liner: Vane is an early-development native macOS web browser built with Swift and WebKit, featuring sidebar tabs, Spaces, and Split View.
summary.what_it_does: Vane is a macOS browser that renders pages with Apple's WKWebView and adds its own organization and reading tools. Its feature set includes sidebar tabs, Favourites, pinned tabs, folders, Spaces, Split View, Peek, and a Reader with an offline article queue. It also offers Easels (notes, drawing, captures and JSON/PNG export), per-site Boosts for styles, and a custom Picture in Picture. Data features cover separate profiles, a local Keychain password store, browser imports, and complete library backups. Integrations include Chrome Web Store extensions, EasyList-subset content blocking, GitHub Live Folders, and optional AI providers using the user's own keys. The README describes the project as in active development and requires macOS 26 or later.
use_cases: browse the web in a native macOS window
read articles offline in a reader view
install Chrome Web Store extensions on a Mac
notable: Sidebar tabs with Spaces, Favourites, and Split View in a single native window
Easels for notes, drawing, page captures, and live web views
Per-site Boosts for injected styles and opt-in scripts
Custom Picture in Picture with a minimized sidebar player
Built on the system WebKit engine rather than a bundled Chromium
caveats: In active development; the README says to read the limitations before using it as your only browser
Requires macOS 26 or later; passkeys are pending Apple entitlement approval and folder uploads are blocked on macOS 27.0.x
Backups are unencrypted, do not sync between Macs, and exclude Keychain secrets, cookies, and downloaded files
keywords: open source browser build from source
